+++ b/debian/patches/upki-openssl-no-issuer.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+From: Shiva Kiran Koninty <shiva.koninty@canonical.com>
+Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:14:15 +0530
+Subject: upki-openssl: Do not fail when the chain has no issuer
+
+upki looks for the issuer of the leaf among the certificates after it, so a
+single-certificate chain (a self-signed certificate errors out, even though
+OpenSSL had already accepted the chain (preverify_ok).
+
+This causes curl to not connect to servers having trusted self-signed
+certificates.
+
+Soft-fail in that case, as the issuer is the leaf itself.
+
+---
+ upki-openssl/src/lib.rs | 6 ++++++
+ 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)
+
+--- a/upki-openssl/src/lib.rs
++++ b/upki-openssl/src/lib.rs
+@@ -151,6 +151,12 @@ pub unsafe extern "C" fn upki_openssl_ve
+             preverify_ok = 0;
+         }
+         upki_result::UPKI_ERR_REVOCATION_FILE_READ | upki_result::UPKI_REVOCATION_NOT_COVERED | upki_result::UPKI_REVOCATION_NOT_REVOKED => {}
++        // The issuer is looked up among the certificates after the leaf, so
++        // single-certificate chains (such as trusted self-signed certs) fail
++        // with `NO_ISSUER`. OpenSSL has already accepted the chain
++        // (`preverify_ok`) and there is no issuer to look up in the revocation
++        // data, so soft-fail.
++        upki_result::UPKI_ERR_REVOCATION_NO_ISSUER => {}
+         _e => {
+             x509_ctx.set_error(X509_V_ERR_APPLICATION_VERIFICATION);
+             preverify_ok = 0;
